purpose: Separate HW6 section 6.2 one-factor-at-a-time PPR demonstration
observations: Setting 1 vs 2: fixed alpha .85 and graph, user 1 to user 2; 0/10 shared movies; mean popularity 245.5 to 254.9. Per-user test filtering also changes; all ten user-2 movies are excluded for user 1.

Setting 1 vs 3: fixed user 1, graph and exclusions, alpha .85 to .50; 7/10 shared movies; mean popularity 245.5 to 228.4. Scream, Air Force One and Titanic leave; Trainspotting, Sense and Sensibility and E.T. enter.
The first six titles keep the same order when alpha changes. Star Trek: First Contact moves from rank 9 to rank 7.
For this user and graph, higher alpha gives the more popular of these two lists. This does not show that either list is better, or that alpha has a universal relationship with popularity.
Scores are long-run walk probabilities. Differences in score magnitudes across alpha settings are not changes in predicted rating or recommendation quality.
These are descriptive demonstrations. The primary final evaluation continues to use validation-selected alpha .50; the demonstrations do not select or replace it.

graph.edgeHashSerialization: Distinct positive training (user_id,movie_id) pairs sorted ascending, each formatted user_id,movie_id plus LF
graph.construction: Binary bidirectional edges for training ratings >= 4.0; missing unobserved

filtering: All 1,611 training-movie candidates; exclude every movie rated in training or validation for that user, regardless of rating value. Descending score, exact ties ascending movie ID.

crossUserFilteringContext.note: Each user has their own standard test exclusion set. All ten setting-2 movies were previously rated by user 1; zero overlap cannot establish a pure restart-seed effect or better personalization.
